Direct answer | This page's Gas Compressor and Gas Pumping Station Operators corresponds to US SOC 53-7071.00, and the work can be divided into several categories: compression and pumping operations — operate compressors and power-driven pumps driven by steam, gas, electric motors or internal combustion engines to convey, compress or recover gases such as butane, nitrogen, hydrogen and natural gas, start and stop units and auxiliary equipment, and adjust valves and equipment to set values; parameter monitoring and adjustment — monitor instruments and pressure gauges to judge changes in consumption rates, temperature and pressure, turn valves and knobs or switches to regulate pressure, and record instrument readings and operating changes in the operating log; sampling, testing and metering — collect gas samples and run chemical tests to determine gas quality and sulfur or water content, or send them to a laboratory for analysis, and read gas meters and record the gas received and distributed by holders; reporting and maintenance — submit daily facility operating reports, clean, lubricate and adjust equipment with hand tools and replace filters and gaskets, and perform general station housekeeping and pipe connections. The four categories cycle in sequence: shift handover and inspection — reading gauges and judging — adjusting or starting and stopping — sampling, metering and recording — handling and reporting anomalies per the real contingency plan. This page does not conflate this position with the adjacent pump operators, gas plant operators or industrial machinery maintenance positions. The fixed index gives this asset the Chinese original name Natural Gas Natural Gas Operator, and the original index is retained; this page explains the occupational meaning based on the official multi-gas scope.

O*NET and BLS occupational profile highlights | This page corresponds to US SOC 53-7071.00 Gas Compressor and Gas Pumping Station Operators (a position under the transportation and material moving major group), with the official scope: operate compressors driven by steam, gas, electric motors or internal combustion engines to convey, compress or recover gases such as butane, nitrogen, hydrogen and natural gas. The core tasks listed by O*NET include: monitor instruments and pressure gauges to judge changes in consumption rates and temperature and pressure; when problems are found, adjust control room equipment or direct other personnel to adjust equipment at the problem location or another control area; record instrument readings and operating changes in the operating log; adjust valves and equipment to achieve specified performance; manipulate controls and turn valves to start compressor engines, pumps and auxiliary equipment; operate power-driven pumps that move liquid, semi-liquid, gas or powder materials; submit daily facility operating reports; collect gas samples and run chemical tests to determine gas quality and sulfur or water content, or send them to a laboratory for analysis; read gas meters and record the gas received and distributed by holders; turn knobs or switches to regulate pressure; clean, lubricate and adjust equipment with hand tools and replace filters and gaskets; perform station housekeeping such as painting, flushing and cleaning; and connect pipes between pumps and containers being filled or emptied. The most important work activities are documenting and recording information (87) and repairing and maintaining mechanical equipment (87), followed by controlling machines and processes (85) and getting information (85).

Boundary conclusion | This page corresponds to US SOC 53-7071.00, and the core difference from adjacent positions lies in the object and the output: this occupation takes the gas in compressor units and pumps and valves and instruments and pipes as its object, and its output is stable, verifiable compression and conveyance operations, parameter records and gas quality and gas volume data; pump operators (except wellhead pumpers, 53-7072) take pumping systems outside the wellhead as their main object; wellhead pumpers (53-7073) take oil well wellhead pumps and metering as their object; stationary engineers and boiler operators (51-8021) take boilers and steam or power equipment and supporting systems as their object; industrial machinery mechanics (49-9041) produce the repair and maintenance of mechanical equipment; control and valve installers and repairers (non-mechanical category, 49-9012) produce the installation, calibration and repair of control and valve devices. The objects and outputs all differ, and equipment adjustment and parameter setting and safety isolation and permit authority cannot be carried over across positions.

Core concept of adjacent positions | Most positions in the group and adjacent positions aim to keep equipment and media and parameters under control per procedures at an industrial site and to be responsible for safety and continuous energy or gas supply; the difference lies in the object and the output: some take compressor units and pipeline gas as the object, some take wellhead pumps and oil well metering as the object, some take boilers and steam and power systems as the object, some produce mechanical equipment repair, and some produce the installation and calibration of control and valve devices.

Core purpose of this occupation | With the gas in compressors and pumps and valves and instruments and pipes as its object, within the bounds of safety and work permits and institutional procedures, convert the gas conveyance and compression of a pipeline network or facility into stable, verifiable operating parameters and gas volume and quality records: shift inspection, reading pressure and temperature and flow, adjustment and start-up and shutdown, sampling and testing and metering, and shutdown, isolation and escalation on anomalies, so that the operating process and parameters are traceable and meet safety and environmental requirements.

Main objects and basis of adjacent positions | Pump operators (except wellhead pumpers) rely on pumping systems and process flows; wellhead pumpers rely on oil well wellhead pumps and production metering; stationary engineers and boiler operators rely on boilers and steam and power equipment and supporting systems; industrial machinery mechanics rely on mechanical equipment repair procedures and plans; control and valve installers and repairers (non-mechanical category) rely on the installation and calibration procedures for control and valve devices.

Main objects and basis of this occupation | The objects are compressors and power-driven pumps and valves and knobs and switches, instruments and pressure gauges and gas meters, pipes and gas holders and containers, gas samples and indicators such as sulfur and water content, and operating logs and daily reports and gas metering records, based on institutional safety procedures and work permits and operating procedures, equipment manufacturer procedures and interlock and alarm settings, and environmental and metering and record requirements.

Occupational profile | This page's gas compressor and gas pumping station operators correspond to US SOC 53-7071.00 (updated by O*NET in 2026), and carry out compression and pumping equipment operations at natural gas long-distance pipeline compressor stations, gas storage facilities, gas processing and conveyance facilities, and wholesale trade and industrial gas links: operate compressors and power-driven pumps driven by steam, gas, electric motors or internal combustion engines to convey, compress or recover gases such as butane, nitrogen, hydrogen and natural gas; monitor instruments and pressure gauges to judge changes in consumption rates and temperature and pressure, adjust valves and equipment to achieve specified performance and record readings and changes in the operating log; collect gas samples and run chemical tests to determine gas quality and sulfur or water content or send them to a laboratory for analysis; read gas meters and record the gas received and distributed by holders and submit daily facility operating reports; and clean, lubricate and adjust equipment with hand tools and replace filters and gaskets. The work is characterized by outdoor and industrial environments, noise and high and low temperatures and dangerous equipment and strict safety procedures, with very high responsibility for the health and safety of others and potentially extremely serious consequences of error; common employers include pipeline transportation and natural gas distribution companies, oil and gas extraction and gas processing and gas storage operators, and industrial gas and wholesale supply links; authority over permits and interlocks and isolation and metering and records is determined by the employer and work permit and regulatory requirements.

Core process of adjacent positions | Pump operators (except wellhead pumpers) focus on pumping system operation and monitoring; wellhead pumpers focus on wellhead pump operation and production metering; stationary engineers and boiler operators focus on boiler and power equipment operation and steam and thermal regulation; industrial machinery mechanics focus on mechanical equipment inspection, repair and replacement; control and valve installers and repairers (non-mechanical category) focus on the installation, calibration and repair of control and valve devices.

Core process of this occupation | Take over the shift and inspect per procedure and check the status of compressor units and valves and instruments, read pressure and temperature and flow and judge deviations, adjust valves and controls or start and stop units and auxiliary pumps, sample and test and read gas meters and meter, and record and hand over in the operating log and daily report; every step must leave a trail per safety procedures and work permits and be reviewable by supervisors and dispatch and maintenance and safety positions.

Main outputs of adjacent positions | Pump operators (except wellhead pumpers) produce pumping system operation and flow and pressure records; wellhead pumpers produce wellhead pump operation and production metering records; stationary engineers and boiler operators produce boiler and power system operation and thermal records; industrial machinery mechanics produce equipment repair and replacement and commissioning results; control and valve installers and repairers produce installation and calibration records for control and valve devices.

Main outputs of this occupation | Stable, verifiable compression and conveyance operations and parameter records (pressure, temperature, flow and consumption rates), start-up and shutdown and switching and adjustment records, gas sample test results and gas metering records, facility daily operating reports and operating logs, and equipment maintenance and replacement and anomaly and handling and handover records.

Responsible parties for adjacent positions | Responsibility for positions in the group and adjacent positions is usually defined by the institution and safety and process procedures and work permits, and the objects of responsibility are mostly the institution and the crew and the safety of others and continuity of gas or energy supply.

Responsible party for this occupation | This occupation is responsible for the operation and parameter adjustment and records of the shift's compression and pumping equipment and for implementing shift safety, and for start-up and shutdown and adjustment and sampling and metering and records completed per procedure; matters involving changes to interlock and alarm settings, overpressure or leak handling, hot work and confined space and work-at-height permits, and equipment repair and replacement and metering settlement are decided by the duty supervisor and dispatch and maintenance and safety positions and the corresponding permits, and this occupation does not replace their decisions.

Adjacent positions likewise judge and act per their own actual equipment procedures and employer authority; it is not inferred that frontline staff may never judge; when authority is exceeded, information is missing or an anomaly procedure is triggered, the matter is handed over per the applicable process.

Within authority, start-up, shutdown, adjustment, sampling, metering and maintenance may be carried out per procedure; changes to protection settings and special operations require separately verified authority, and missing information or out-of-scope matters are escalated per the rules. General descriptions cannot grant authority to bypass interlocks, perform maintenance under pressure or settle metering.

Conclusion boundaries of adjacent positions | Conclusions for positions in the group and adjacent positions are mostly limited to the shift and the position and the equipment level and usually do not constitute a final determination of equipment integrity, media safety or metering settlement; conclusions across units and sites and institutions have limits to their applicability.

On-shift conclusions distinguish original readings, calculations, inferences and unknowns; judgments within authority follow the real procedures, and out-of-authority and missing conditions are verified separately. A book difference is not directly determined to be a leak, and a proposed report is not written as received.

The objects and outputs all differ, and equipment adjustment and parameter setting and safety isolation and work permit authority cannot be carried over across positions.

The six directions are edited and compared by the focus of object and output and may overlap; actual wages, entry requirements and authority are verified separately, and no sales material is treated as an official factual basis.

Preface | The following comparison is laid out in four columns: career direction — core work and outputs — key differences — which choice suits better. Compression and pumping, control and valves, mechanical repair, gas processing, pumping outside the wellhead, and boiler and power systems often connect within the same industrial site, but connection does not mean they are interchangeable; when choosing across directions you should re-learn the equipment principles, safety procedures and work permit and authority scope.

This occupation centers on compression and conveyance operations, and the 13 core tasks also include mechanical maintenance and power pump tasks, so it is not absolutely mutually exclusive with repair or other pump positions; duties and authority are determined by the specific position, not the name.

Better suited to people who are willing to inspect and read gauges per procedure in outdoor and industrial environments, maintain attention under noise and high and low temperatures and dangerous equipment, and consistently wear protective equipment and strictly follow safety procedures and work permits.

Core work and outputs: take over the shift and inspect and check the status of compressor units and valves and instruments and pressure gauges, read pressure and temperature and flow and judge deviations, adjust valves and controls or start and stop units and auxiliary pumps, collect gas samples and test quality and sulfur or water content or send them for testing, read gas meters and record the gas received and distributed by holders, submit daily facility operating reports, and clean, lubricate and adjust equipment and replace filters and gaskets; the outputs are stable, verifiable compression and conveyance operations and parameter and gas volume and quality records and daily operating reports (US SOC 53-7071.00).
This occupation: Gas Compressor and Gas Pumping Station Operators (53-7071.00)

Control valve installation, calibration and repair are the focus; this occupation performs authorized maintenance adjustments during operation, the two may overlap, and it cannot be inferred that this occupation never maintains valves.

Better suited to people willing to take responsibility for the installation, calibration and repair of control and valve devices; this occupation leans more toward the operation and parameter adjustment and recording of compression and pumping equipment.

Core work and outputs: install, calibrate and repair control and valve devices used to regulate and control fluid flow and pressure (flow meters, control valves, safety valves, pressure regulators and pneumatic or electric actuators), read and verify instruments, check for leaks and operation and record; the outputs are installation, calibration and repair records for control and valve devices.
Control and Valve Installers and Repairers, Except Mechanical Door (49-9012.00)

Industrial machinery repair focuses on inspection and diagnosis; for this occupation cleaning, lubrication and adjustment and filter and gasket replacement are core tasks, and whether major overhaul is involved is verified separately per the real position.

Better suited to people willing to take responsibility for mechanical equipment repair and preventive maintenance and fault diagnosis; this occupation leans more toward equipment operation and parameter adjustment and recording.

Core work and outputs: inspect, lubricate, adjust and repair mechanical equipment (compressors, pumps, drive and shaft systems and seals) on a plan, diagnose fault signals such as vibration, temperature, sound and leaks, disassemble and inspect and replace parts and run trial tests; the outputs are mechanical equipment repair and preventive maintenance and trial run records.
Industrial Machinery Mechanics (49-9041.00)

Key differences: gas plant operators produce the unit and process operation and product specifications of gas processing and distribution facilities (dehydration, desulfurization, fractionation, pressure regulation and metering, odorization and so on), with a broader unit scope; this occupation centers on the operation of compression and pumping equipment and usually does not take responsibility for whole-process adjustment and product specifications.

Better suited to people willing to take responsibility for whole-process process operation and product specifications of gas processing and distribution; this occupation leans more toward equipment operation and parameter records of compressor units and pumping stations.

Core work and outputs: operate and control gas processing and distribution units, adjust process parameters and product specifications, monitor and handle process anomalies, sample and test and record product and process data; the outputs are gas products meeting specifications and process operation and records.
Gas Plant Operators (51-8092.00)

Pump operators have a broader range of media and scenarios; this occupation's core tasks also list power-driven pumps conveying liquid, semi-liquid, gas or powder, so it cannot be said that it only handles gas and never operates non-gas pumps.

Better suited to people willing to take responsibility for the operation and monitoring of multi-media pumping systems; this occupation leans more toward gas compression and pumping and sampling and metering.

Core work and outputs: operate and monitor power-driven pumps outside the wellhead with their valves and instruments to convey liquid, semi-liquid, gas or powder, regulate flow and pressure and record operating and metering data; the outputs are pumping system operation and flow and pressure and metering records.
Pump Operators, Except Wellhead Pumpers (53-7072.00)

Key differences: stationary engineers and boiler operators produce the operation and thermal regulation of boilers and steam and power equipment, involving combustion and steam and thermal systems; this occupation takes gas compressors and pumps as its object and usually does not take responsibility for the operation of boiler and steam systems.

Better suited to people willing to take responsibility for the operation and thermal regulation of boiler and steam and power systems; this occupation leans more toward gas compression and pumping equipment operation.

Core work and outputs: operate and monitor boilers and steam and power equipment with their pumps, valves and instruments, regulate combustion and water level and pressure and temperature, handle anomalies and record operating and maintenance data; the outputs are steam and power system operation and thermal and maintenance records.
Stationary Engineers and Boiler Operators (51-8021.00)

Transition | This page places adjacent positions side by side by object and output so that you can judge which kind of industrial site equipment operation or installation and repair or process and power position you want to invest in long term. Whichever direction you choose, what really decides whether you can start is your understanding of equipment principles and safety procedures and work permits, your ability to get parameters and records right and complete, and passing the institution's safety training and medical examination and qualification confirmation; interest questionnaires are only used to raise questions.

subject.name: Gas Compressor and Gas Pumping Station Operators
subject.summary: Operate compressors and power-driven pumps to convey, compress or recover gases such as butane, nitrogen, hydrogen and natural gas; monitor instruments, adjust equipment per procedures and authority, and record operating changes, gas volumes and sampling results. On-site operation, anomaly handling and maintenance authority are verified separately per the actual position.
